submitted.rationale: EQE rose steeply as Fe content increased: 0.0056% at Fe 0.49 (FeSbO4), 0.229% at Fe 0.74, and 0.544% at Fe 0.83. The Fe-rich films are likely hematite with some Sb in it or mixed with FeSbO4. Index 1 had the highest EQE of the three measurements.

rejected.reason: Near-1:1 FeSbO4 is stable and predicted to absorb, but measured EQE was only 0.0056%
Not measured because the merit budget ran out; the trend suggests it could be similar or slightly better

consultations.verdict: Support: rutile FeSbO4 is on the MACE hull (0.002 eV/atom) with predicted HSE gap 2.08 eV < 2.7 eV photon energy, so near-1:1 composition (index 12) should form a single absorbing phase.

Support (moderate): hematite is on the MACE hull, so Fe-rich films should be hematite + FeSbO4 composites; hematite absorbs at 2.7 eV (experimental gap ~2.1 eV even though MEGNet says 2.77), and FeSbO4 alone measured near-zero EQE, so move to Fe-rich side (index 5, Fe 0.74).

Uninformative-to-supportive: MEGNet gaps for hematite vary widely by fidelity (0.8 SCAN vs 2.8 HSE), so they can't pin down absorption. Hematite is still the stable Fe-rich absorber. The measured trend (EQE 0.0056 at Fe 0.49 vs 0.229 at Fe 0.74) favours going more hematite-rich, so I'm measuring index 1 (Fe 0.83).
